title: _photo_meta.json
description: Provenance for real photographs. One file per asset folder, keyed by filename, sitting beside the images it describes. Validated by scripts/check_assets.py.

source.description: organisation or repository the file came from

url_or_origin.description: page URL, or the project path for a PROJECT_OWNED asset

licence.description: e.g. CC BY-SA 4.0, CC0, public domain, written permission

cleared_by.description: 2.63.2 (L52): a source-book figure ships only on a named person's decision - "<name>, <YYYY-MM-DD> - <reason>", with rights_state OWNER_CLEARED and source_work. Set by `check_assets.py clear`, never automatically. Without a whole cleared_by the figure stays blocked (check_assets FAIL, never an L57 thumbnail)

source_work.description: a source-book figure's real source: book, edition, page / figure. It is its credit in the full-screen view and on the course's credits page (unless a `credit` is written)

credit.description: the credit shown for a cleared source-book figure; `check_assets.py clear` writes source_work here when empty

description.description: what the photograph LITERALLY shows - not what it is used to teach. Trainees read it: full screen shows it under the photo on every slide (L51, L56, gb_zoom.js), so write it for them - what is in the picture and where to look, in plain words, never more than the picture evidences

shows.description: L57: the plain names of the on-board things the photograph really shows, as slides and drawings name them, lower case, no abbreviations - e.g. ["fuel tank", "type C tank"], ["bunkering station"]. The compiler puts the photo beside every drawing that names one of them. Only what the picture evidences: a cargo tank of an LNG carrier is a "membrane tank", never a "fuel tank"

generated.description: true for a picture made by an image model (nano banana and the like): the record stays (provenance), but it shows no credit line and no label on screen (operator, 2026-10-15) and is never placed as an L57 thumbnail. Record 'generator', 'prompt' and 'approved_by_user' (L47) with it

generator.description: the image model that made a generated picture, for the record, e.g. 'Nano Banana (Google Gemini image model)' - not shown on screen

copied_from.description: set by the compiler when it copied the photo in from another module of the course (L57)

visually_verified.description: 'yes - <what was seen> <date>', or a plain statement that it was not verified. Never 'yes' for a file nobody opened.

caption_caveat.description: an honest near-miss note, e.g. 'a product tanker, not a gas carrier'
